title: Machine learning guides engineering of an alkaloid-biosynthesis enzyme
summary: Researchers developed MutComputeX, a structure-based residual neural network for assessing amino-acid substitutions in protein–ligand environments, and used it with a 4′-O-methylnorbelladine biosensor to engineer the plant methyltransferase Nb4OMT in Escherichia coli. The paper reports engineered variants with 60% higher product titer, twofold higher catalytic activity, threefold lower off-product regioisomer formation and 5 °C higher thermostability; ligand-aware predictions helped identify the beneficial A53M substitution. These enzyme and product results do not demonstrate complete microbial production of galantamine.
ai_technology: MutComputeX structure-based residual neural network for protein–ligand mutation design

evidence.tested: MutComputeX-guided, manually curated Nb4OMT variants were assayed using a 4NB biosensor and biochemical methods. The article reports 60% higher product titer, twofold higher catalytic activity, threefold lower off-product formation and 5 °C higher thermostability for engineered variants.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns a pathway enzyme and branchpoint intermediate in the reported microbial/biochemical systems; full pathway production of galantamine and industrial manufacturing were not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: MutComputeX predicted sequence substitutions in a modeled protein–ligand microenvironment and guided selection of Nb4OMT variants for biosensor screening and enzyme assays; ligand-aware predictions supported A53M.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications full text as indexed, including methods/results, author contributions and affiliation block.
